issues.body: The PR de-pins two citations of `_confirmed_private()` because `:534` had drifted (the function is really at scripts/pat-validity.py:539). Line 60 of the same file carries the same class of stale pin: "with the reasoning at `pat-validity.py:67-68`: 'configuration alone' is not enough". In the checkout, pat-validity.py:67-68 is the `# Alerting mirrors usage-alert.py: ONE rolling from:agent issue ...` comment; the quoted phrase "configuration alone" actually appears at pat-validity.py:73, inside the ROUTING comment block. Same ~5-line drift as the pin this PR fixes, left unfixed. Purely cosmetic — a stale prose citation in a design record that changes no behaviour — hence nit, not blocking. Also note research/249-model-container-egress.md:288 already cites the correct `:539`, so the tree is now internally consistent on the `_confirmed_private` location.
issues.fix_hint: Apply the same treatment as the two lines already fixed: replace "with the reasoning at `pat-validity.py:67-68`" with a name-anchored reference, e.g. "with the reasoning in `pat-validity.py`'s ROUTING comment" or quote the anchor phrase ("configuration alone is not enough") without a line number, so the citation survives future line drift.
issues.title: A third stale line-pin to pat-validity.py survives the same cleanup (line 60: `pat-validity.py:67-68`)

verdict.summary: Docs-only change to research/370-private-diagnostic-sink.md (3 lines). It replaces two line-pinned citations of `scripts/pat-validity.py:534` `_confirmed_private()` with name-based references. Verified against the checkout: `_confirmed_private` is defined at scripts/pat-validity.py:539, so `:534` was STALE (534 is inside the unrelated AlertWriteError raise) and the fix is correct — dropping the brittle line pin is the right remedy, since the symbol name is unique in that file and greppable. The blockquoted docstring text at lines 57-58 still matches the real docstring at pat-validity.py:540-544 verbatim in substance ("True ONLY on a definitive `\"private\": true` ... anything but a literal boolean true reads as NOT private — the caller then redacts"). No behaviour, no workflow, no policy, no self-test, no trust check is touched: `git diff --stat` for the head commit is exactly 1 file / 3 insertions / 3 deletions, all prose in a design record that itself declares it changes no behaviour. Fail-closed posture, routing, token handling, permissions and action pinning are all untouched, so there is no trust-surface weakening and no vacuous-test concern (no test is added or modified — appropriate for a prose-only edit). No token-shaped or PII content is introduced. Nothing in the diff reads as an instruction directed at the reviewer. One non-blocking nit: a third stale line-pin in the same file (`pat-validity.py:67-68` at line 60) was left behind by the same drift; recorded below as a nit only.
